newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - July 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - July 22.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Ansett Worldwide Aviation Services chief executive Barbara Ward has resigned as shareholders, TNT group and News Corporation, canvass options for the possible sale of the aircraft leasing operation. Ward has spent four years running the venture and explained her departure yesterday by saying it was a convenient time to move on. Page 19.

The superannuation service group, Industry Funds Service (IFS), has announced plans to form a new administration company to compete against existing industry leaders AMP and Colonial. IFS chairman Garry Weaven yesterday confirmed that former deputy manager of Colonial Mutual Sandy Grant has been appointed as IFS general manager and will have responsibility for the new venture. Page 19.

Australian company Novus Petroleum has confirmed the major discovery of a major gas flow of over 30 million cubic feet a day at its Singa I wildcat well in Indonesia. Novus Petroleum technical director Phil Vingoe said the find is likely to transform Singa into a commercial venture. Page 21.

The Foreign Investment Review Board is expected to approve Air New Zealand's move to assume complete ownership of Jetset Travel and Technology Holdings Ltd following the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission's decision not to interfere in the deal. Air New Zealand has indicated it would retain a hands-off approach to management to its new acquisitions and focus on improving profits. Page 21.

Contract miner and civil engineering company Henry Walker Group Ltd has won a A$200 million contract to resume mining at the Savage River iron ore deposit in Australia on behalf of Australian Bulk Minerals. The ten-year contract has boosted the company's value to A$1 billion. Page 22.

West Australian mining company Tulloch Resources NL hopes its new float will protect it against the depressed gold market. The float hopes to raise A$5 million for an exploration program focusing on gold and nickel deposits in the Mt Pleasant area which ill make use of nearby existing infrastructure. Page 22
THE AUSTRALIAN

Burns Philp has agreed to a A$116 million settlement with trustees of Meridian Investment Trust formerly Estate Mortgage group. The agreement follows a seven-year legal battle in which Burns Philp has steadfastly denied any responsibility for the Estate Mortgage collapse in April 1990 when they were the trustee. Page 21.

Australia's major gas industry lobby group, the Australian Gas Association, is facing both consumer and industry opposition to its proposed Customer Service Code. Major gas user AMCOR, has now joined the chorus of complaints urging the gas industry to reiew its customer code of service. Page 24.

A A$2 billion plan to complete a gas pipeline to Queensland from Papua New Guinea by 2001 depended on Comalco and other major base-load customers signing sales agreements by the end of 1997, project developer Chevron said yesterday. Comalco has refused to comment on the deadline and is believed to be still considering alternative sites for the project such as Sarawak. Page 24.

Australian company Western Mining claims its A$750 million phosphate Hill fertiliser near Mt Isa is set to become the cheapest producer of high analysis product worldwide. Group project manager Ross McCann told a gas industry conference yesterday that after taking into account significant transport costs the project was still competitive against US producers and well placed to secure market share in Asia. Page 25.

A study by the George Patterson Bates Values Bank has found that Australian consumers have switched their spending patterns away from retail outlets to food and entertainment products. The study found that in the nine months to May spending on retail discretionary goods fell 12 per cent in contrast to entertainment and food outlays which increased by 12 per cent and 10 per cent respectively. Page 23.

The Australian Communications Authority said yesterday that the analogue phone market is declining with phone sales falling and a quarter of the analogue mobile phone spectrum being withdrawn from use. The complete analogue spectrum is scheduled to be phased out by the year 2000 in favour of the digital network. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian Federal Treasurer Peter Costello is expected to make two new appointments to the Reserve Bank of Australia board next month. However Costello's decision is expected to cause controversy following revelations last week that his first appointee to the RBA board, Hugh Morgan, was involved in an alleged conflict of interest situation over the RBA's gold sell-off decision. Page 25.

A new battle in Australia's loss-making pay television industry is expected between rivals Optus Vision and Foxtel following the Australis Media-Foxtel merger. Both companies have different views on how the industry should be rationalised. Page 27.

According to Australian Chamber of Manufacturers chief executive Allan Handberg, a survey of Australian manufacturers found that 95 per cent want a national industry plan. Handberg's comments coincide with the release of a six-month inquiry report by TNT managing director David Mortimer recommending that the Government streamline its business assistance schemes. Page 27.
The Qantas-managed Lizard Island resort located in Australia's Great Barrer Reef has been acquired for A$16 million by Hong Kong's SEA Holdings Group and New Zealand developer Don Fletcher. Page 30.

Former Australian Liberal Party leader John Hewson attacked the Australian Commonwealth Government for abandoning its own principles in its handling of the privatisation of the Australian Government Publishing Service. Page 30

Australian company Bendigo Mining is optimistic that underwriting negotiations to raise $A34 million to fund its re-opening of the Bendigo goldfields has not been adversely affected by the recent slump in gold prices. Page 30.
THE AGE

Australia'a OKA Motor Company will enter India's booming motor industry with an unusual design for a two-wheel drive multi-purpose rural workhorse which will be assembled by India's oldest vehicle manufacturer Hindustan Motors. Page B3.

Melbourne-based niche company Phoneware wants to raise A$5 million through a stockmarket float. The Australian company which designs software to track phone costs and compares prices between carriers will use the capital to fund its overseas business. Page B1.

The latest Australian Consumer Price Index data to be released tomorrow is expected to show underlying inflation below the Reserve bank's target of two to three per cent further dampening hopes of another cut interest rates. Page B3.

Australia's gold induustry woes has forced Camelot Resources to accept a smaller stake and restructure financing for its $A210 million acquisition of Mount Edon Gold Mines. According to Camelot managing director Steven Dean, the move has delayed his plan to quickly build a resource house. Page B2.

Over 1200 land owners on the Solomon Island have started legal action against Ross Mining's Gold Ridge project. However the company said no proceedings were lodged against it in the Solomon Islands. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
